segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּיָּיתוֹת לוֹקְחִין מֵהֶן, מִדְבָּרִיּוֹת אֵין לוֹקְחִין מֵהֶן כּוּ׳. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – אַרֵישָׁא קָאֵי, וּלְחוּמְרָא; אוֹ דִלְמָא אַסֵּיפָא קָאֵי, וּלְקוּלָּא?
segments.en: The baraita teaches that «Rabbi Yehuda says: One may purchase domesticated» animals «from them,» but «one may not purchase desert» animals «from them. A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: Is the statement of «Rabbi Yehuda referring to the first clause, and» his statement is therefore «a stringency? Or perhaps» it «is referring to the latter clause, and» his statement is «a leniency?»
